prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

For systems that are severely damaged or can no longer operate normally, reconstruction shall be carried out according to actual needs. 4.3 Urban Furniture 4.3.1 Traffic Management Facilities The color, form, style, and other aspects of traffic management facilities in the same city should be as unified as possible; roads in certain special areas may be designed with appropriate distinctive features. 1. Traffic facility poles: When traffic management facilities such as traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards are arranged in the median/side median, they shall be aligned with the centerline of streetlights and other facilities within the median. Where there is no side median or central median, traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards shall be arranged within the sidewalk facility zone and shall not occupy or obstruct sidewalk passage or the area adjacent to pedestrian crosswalk lines. Traffic facility poles should, as far as possible, achieve “one pole for multiple uses.” When streetlight poles and sign poles are combined into one pole, full consideration shall be given to the issue of traffic signs being obscured by the light below (“lamp-shadow blindness”), and the relationship among various poles and roadside trees shall be coordinated comprehensively to avoid roadside trees obstructing signs, monitoring devices, and traffic signal lights. 2. Central median guardrails and side median guardrails: Their layout should start from the stop line at intersections and shall not hinder normal vehicle movement. End warning signs shall be set at the starting point, and reflectors, reflective film, etc. shall be installed on the posts. The length and height of each guardrail panel shall take into account functional requirements, manufacturing process, and the requirements of the deployment area. Figure 4.3-1 Example of Central Median Guardrail 3. Pedestrian guardrails shall start from the end position of the sidewalk curb ramp and be laid close to the inner edge line of the curb. For guardrails at locations with fall hazards, the clear spacing of vertical members shall not be greater than 0.11 m, and structures with footholds are not recommended. Pedestrian guardrails that are not fully isolating or serve a warning function may adopt a post-and-chain form. 4. Vehicle-stopping bollards / vehicle-blocking stones: Materials shall be selected according to the location and functional requirements, using durable materials such as stone, cast iron, stainless steel, galvanized steel, or aluminum alloy. The spacing between bollards should be 1.3 m–1.5 m, and the height should be 0.4 m–0.6 m. Reflective film, warning lights, etc. shall be installed. 151 Figure 4.3-2 Example of Vehicle-Stopping Bollards / Vehicle-Blocking Stones 5. Outdoor municipal boxes and decorative covers: These are generally arranged in public facility zones and roadside green belts, and shall not be arranged on intersection sidewalks, at entrances and exits of residential communities and commercial facilities, or in the sight triangle area of intersections, so as not to affect road traffic. As a city streetscape evaluation expert, please analyze the uploaded streetscape image based on the specified persona perspective and evaluation indicators, and return a JSON result.
 Persona Selection
Road User Type
- All Road Users
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Drivers
Socially Vulnerable Groups
- All Social Groups
- Persons with Disabilities
- Adolescents (<18)
- Older Adults (≥60)
Current Selection:
All Road Users; All Social Groups
 Indicator Selection
Justice
- Equity
- Fairness
- Accessibility
Safety
Livability
Sustainability
Aesthetics
Comfort
- Thermal Comfort
- Physical Comfort
- Psychological Comfort
Walkability
Bikeability
Selected Indicators:
Justice; Safety; Livability; Sustainability; Aesthetics; Comfort; Walkability
 1. Evaluation Dimensions
Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.
 2. Persona Perspective Requirements:
The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:
Persons with Disabilities: Focus on curb ramps, continuity of tactile paving (blind tracks), and physical obstacles.
Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).
 3. How to use the image vs retrieved knowledge:
- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.
 4. Output Format Requirements (Return JSON ONLY, no extra text):

Traffic facility poles: When traffic management facilities such as traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards are arranged in the median/side median, they shall be aligned with the centerline of streetlights and other facilities within the median. Where there is no side median or central median, traffic signal lights, traffic monitoring poles, and traffic sign boards shall be arranged within the sidewalk facility zone and shall not occupy or obstruct sidewalk passage or the area adjacent to pedestrian crosswalk lines. Traffic facility poles should, as far as possible, achieve “one pole for multiple uses.” When streetlight poles and sign poles are combined into one pole, full consideration shall be given to the issue of traffic signs being obscured by the light below (“lamp-shadow blindness”), and the relationship among various poles and roadside trees shall be coordinated comprehensively to avoid roadside trees obstructing signs, monitoring devices, and traffic signal lights. 2. Central median guardrails and side median guardrails: Their layout should start from the stop line at intersections and shall not hinder normal vehicle movement. End warning signs shall be set at the starting point, and reflectors, reflective film, etc. shall be installed on the posts. The length and height of each guardrail panel shall take into account functional requirements, manufacturing process, and the requirements of the deployment area.
